patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Five9 and respond.io share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs. Choose Five9 only if your buying job matches “Cloud contact center (CCaaS) — Digital from $119/concurrent seat/mo; Core $159; Plus/Pro/E” rather than respond.io's shape. Choose respond.io only if your buying job matches “Omnichannel customer messaging platform (WhatsApp + other channels) with shared inbox and ” rather than Five9's shape. Workflow advantage: Five9 leans contact-center, sales-calling; respond.io leans whatsapp-support. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Five9 and respond.io share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: Five9 is Cloud contact center (CCaaS) — Digital from $119/concurrent seat/mo; Core $159; Plus/Pro/Enterprise quote — 50-seat minimum.; respond.io is Omnichannel customer messaging platform (WhatsApp + other channels) with shared inbox and AI — Starter from $79/month annual-equivalent..
- Company-size focus: Five9 (mid-market, enterprise) vs respond.io (small-business, mid-market, enterprise).
- Workflow coverage skew: Five9-leaning contact-center, sales-calling vs respond.io-leaning whatsapp-support.
- Researched limits: Five9 — 50 concurrent-seat minimum — not viable for small SMB phone buyers; respond.io — Not a business phone system — no IVR, queues or PSTN calling product.

Limitations — Five9: 50 concurrent-seat minimum — not viable for small SMB phone buyers; Digital is non-voice; Core is the published voice+digital entry; respond.io: Not a business phone system — no IVR, queues or PSTN calling product; Platform subscription plus channel/Meta messaging fees create two-layer TCO.

Poor-fit cases: Five9 is a poor fit when that limitation bites: 50 concurrent-seat minimum — not viable for small SMB phone buyers · respond.io is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Not a business phone system — no IVR, queues or PSTN calling product · Avoid Five9 if you actually need respond.io's motion (Omnichannel customer messaging platform (WhatsApp + other channels) with shared )

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
